sentences.text: Shri Amit Bhurrak - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/Sta Heard on I.A. No.6387 of 2024 - the second application filed under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant - Kanhaiyalal Markam.
His first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 30.06.2023.
2. Prosecution story in brief is that accused married Sharda Bai (since deceased) in October 2013 and they were living as husband and wife.
On 22.05.2014 at about 11.00 P.M. Sharda Bai (since deceased) got burnt in suspicious condition and succumbed death.
The parents of the deceased lodged complaint against the appellant.

On the basis of the complaint, offences under Sections 363,
366(A), 376(2)(f), 376(2)(n) r/w 304-B & 302 of IPC were registered at Crime No. 218/14 against the appellant.
3. This time the application is filed on the ground of delay in filing the complaint.
It is submitted that appellant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He has not committed any offence in any manner.
He is in custody since 24.11.2022.
He is ready to abide with all the conditions which may be imposed by this Court while considering this appeal.
On these grounds he prays for grant of bail to the appellant.

4. Per contra, learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State opposed the applications and submitted that judgment of impugned conviction is based on proper appreciation of oral as well as documentary evidence.

He has pointed out to the statement of Ranglal (PW/4) who is the father of the deceased wherein he has specifically stated that the narrated to him that the appellant poured kerosene and set her ablaze.

Dr.Mukesh Tilgam (PW/22) also stated that the deceased was 80-90%
burnt when she was brought to the hospital.
The death was homicidal in nature.
Therefore, he has prayed for dismissal of the application.

5. Keeping in view the overall facts and circumstances of the case, coupled with the fact that a specific statement has been made by Ranglal - PW/4 against the appellant in his statement before Kanhaiyalal Markam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9669518/

6. The application (I.A.No.6387 of 2024) is accordingly rejected.
7. List for final hearing in due course.
